blogs.title: The Guideline Gap: Treating Prosthetic Valve Endocarditis When Surgery is Contraindicated
blogs.description: This post analyzes the tension between ESC 2025 guidelines recommending surgical intervention for prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE) versus the clinical reality of prohibitive surgical risk in patients with transcatheter history. It explores how the 'forced' TAVI strategy manages infected bioprosthetic valves and highlights the need for individualized heart team decision-making when open surgery is unsafe.

blogs.title: More Than a Scan: Strategic CT Planning for Triple-Stent Anatomy
blogs.description: Focusing on the critical role of pre-procedural multislice CT (MSCT) in the TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV setting. This clinical teaching point details how specific metric analysis—coronal ostia height, frame interaction, and neo-skirt formation—guides the procedural decision to avoid catastrophic coronary obstruction and ensures anatomical feasibility in complex redo procedures.

blogs.title: The Coronary 'Skyline' Risk: Pre-empting Occlusion in Serial Valve Implantation
blogs.description: A deep dive into the specific anatomical mechanics that pose the highest risk for coronary artery obstruction during serial valve placements. This post scrutinizes the interaction between the neo-skirt of a third-generation valve and previously implanted frames, offering a technical strategy centered on high-implantation positioning to preserve coronary perfusion and access for future life-saving interventions.

blogs.title: The PPM Paradox: Hemodynamic Realities in Cumulative Valve Stacking
blogs.description: Investigating Prosthesis-Patient Mismatch (PPM) as a progressive risk factor in serial TAVI interventions. This analysis contrasts the immediate post-procedural severe gradients with the improved hemodynamics seen at one-year follow-up, discussing the impact of post-dilation, commissural alignment, and effective orifice area calculations on long-term functional outcomes in high-stenosis patients.

blogs.title: Beyond the 'One-and-Done': Lifetime Management and the 'Re-Intervention Pipeline'
blogs.description: Challenging the traditional 'one-and-done' expectation of TAVI for improved longevity patients. This post discusses the strategic implications of multiple valve layers on future procedural complexity, advocating for a long-term surveillance curriculum that explicitly plans for the cardiovascular trajectory of the patient beyond the initial implantation.
